utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. For the Prosecution, Tom Hannis and Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, Aleksandar Aleksic for the Defence of Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Would the usher please escort the witness to the stand. There was something you had, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I had two brief matters. I can do them at the end of the day or I can do them now, whatever is your pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Because we expect this to be a relatively short sitting, perhaps the end of the day would be -- that's more efficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. And for the record I note we are sitting without Judge Harhoff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, good morning to you. Before Mr. Zecevic wraps up his re-examination, I give you a final reminder as to your solemn declaration. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we discussed P199, which is tab 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have on our screens P199, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes and tape-recording of the National Assembly of Republika Srpska held between the 24th and 26th July 1992. At this Assembly Mr. Karadzic gave a speech, gave a presentation, and Mr. Hannis asked you about the order of the Presidency based on which the order of the minister of the interior was adopted to disband all special units in July of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to page 13. In your version it's page 14 of the Serbian text and page 16 of the English text. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph starting with the words: "One of the essential problems ..." It's also the last paragraph in the English text. And Mr. Karadzic says there: "One of the essential problems we are facing is the poor functioning of central authorities. The responsibility lays partly or mostly on us, primarily because we have not yet fully defined the status of SAO autonomous regions, or their organs in relation to the central authorities." Further on at the very end Mr. Karadzic says: "We will know immediately that this is about the congenital Serb tendency towards autonomy, tendency of creating small princedoms and small princes behind whom one can always find private interest and not the interest of the nation." Mr. Macar, in your view, is Mr. Karadzic in these words accurately portraying the situation as it existed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to the next page now, which is page 15 in the English -- no, I apologise, 15 in the Serbian text in e-court and page 17 in the English text.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, somewhere in the middle of the English text, he says, third sentence: "There are only individual needs for power among local power-mongers for power and financial benefit and financial power, which can only temporarily wear the disguise identifying with the motherland, identifying with a smaller entity. I think that history could not deny us any minor identification right now. All Serbs at this point need to identify themselves with the Serbdom in its entirety." On the following page, which is page 16 of the Serbian text and page 18 of the English text, in the middle of the page. Somewhere towards the end of the English text it begins with the words: "However, in the domestic political sense ..." which is somewhere in the middle of the Serbian text. Mr. Karadzic says: "However, in the internal domestic political sense, we have enormous problems, which this Assembly will have to define, that is to say, to give carte blanche to the Presidency and the government to implement decisively the necessary measures in every stage. At this stage the priority is to put into order the state mechanisms of power, that is to say, state organs; to reorient the police for peace time; to place the remaining police force within the JNA; and to place all special police forces which are being misused by some people under the single command of the Republic MUP, and under no circumstances should they be put under the command of some local princes." Tell me, please, Mr. Macar, are you familiar with the fact that this was the position of the president of the Presidency of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and his position was partly formulated based on the information delivered by the ministry, sent by the ministry to the government and to the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one more quotation from the speech. It begins on this page, the last sentence, and then it continues on to the next page which is page 17 of the Serbian text and page 19 of the English text. Somewhere in the middle of the English text it says: "Everything that is being adopted by various Crisis Staffs and various War Presidencies, all of those are measures that are adopted in the state of war and they are not legitimate when adopted by the legal organs of power. This is why I recommend that the Assembly confirm what the Presidency acting as the Assembly has decided, namely, to establish elected and legitimate organs of civilian power everywhere, throughout the territory, and these authorities should not function as rivals of the military power. Rather, they should complement each other." Then he goes on to say: "What is important is that we have to decisively eliminate para-state as well as paramilitary formations. The para-state ones are perhaps even more dangerous right now because they can make catastrophic decisions that in peace time nobody would recognise or confirm, and in the meantime they're causing us great damage." Do you agree with these words of Mr. Karadzic? Do you agree that this reflects the situation as it existed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Following Mr. Karadzic, Branko Djeric, prime minister, also gave a speech. It's your page 17 and page 18 in e-court, whereas page 20 in the English text, 20 and 21. These are the words of Branko Djeric, the prime minister. And then on the following page, page 19 in e-court and page 21 of the English text, Mr. Djeric gives a comment at the bottom. It begins with the words "certainly" or "naturally." It is also in the middle in the English text "the geographical seat of the government ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJERIC SAYS
utterances.text: "Certainly their contribution but a negative contribution came as a result of the geographical seat of the government. Namely, due to the conflict and other factors, the government was for a longer period of time completely isolated, had no contacts and no co-operation with the municipalities. SAO Krajina and SAO Herzegovina were for a while completely cut off from the government and had no contact with the government." Sir, these are the words of the prime minister. What was the experience of the minister of the interior, was it similar to what he's saying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And at the end of his presentation, Mr. Djeric, as prime minister, on your page 23, gives proposals for measures that the government wants the Assembly to adopt. In e-court in the Serbian version it's page 24 and page 26 in English, which is item 2 of his proposals. I apologise, 25 in English. And then it continues on to 26, but it begins on page 25. Item 2 reads: "While the war conflict is on and while the fight for freedom is on, ensure strengthening of central authorities to the necessary level. It is necessary to adopt a decision today to bring about constitutional amendments to proclaim, among other things, the title of the Serb Republic and the Republic's political and territorial organisation." And then on the following page, page 25 of the Serbian version, he says: "In doing so, the current administrations of SAO would become the administrations of regions." Mr. Macar, Mr. Djeric here proposes constitutional amendments. Do you know whether these amendments were eventually adopted and what were they about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Autonomous regions were abolished -- rather, their responsibilities and their jurisdiction were abolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the same page, item 4, another proposal to the Assembly was to issue or implementation of the order of the Presidency on the ground and the order on withdrawing paramilitary formations and placing all formations and reserve police under single military command. Are you familiar with this instruction, with this proposal, rather, of the government given to the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about this. And earlier on when I said that Mr. Djeric was not all that familiar with state administration, I should have given an explanation, or rather, an explanation is needed here, that if there are any extra military -- rather, if there are any extra police reserve forces, they should be put under the military command. That was the gist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The last proposal under item 7: "The government seeks support for placing," or rather, "for vacating immediately all regulations and all enactments adopted at all municipal levels or adopted by certain state organs which are contrary to the constitution, laws, and other regulations of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina or else they need to be put into compliance." Sir, can you tell me which regulations does the government have in mind here when making this proposal?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They primarily refer to regulations which deal with the work of the state administration, so as not to enumerate starting from the constitution, the Law on State Administration and Local Administration. And they mean that there needs to be a harmonisation between the local regulations and constitution as well as the legislation passed at the level of the Serbian republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as not to lose any more time, I'll just give reference to the Trial Chamber. P2308, tab -- 2038, tab 116 has the conclusions and the decisions of the Assembly which pertain to these proposals advanced by the president of the Presidency and prime minister. This is under items 3, 5, 6, and 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have no more than two or three questions left. Page 23413 of the LiveNote, Mr. Hannis showed you P2016 which can be found at OTP tab 95. You don't have that in front of you, sir, but it will come up on your screen. This was about the appointment of Vojin Popovic as chief of the Gacko public security station. You remember commenting on that when prompted by Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 1D323 is our next document, please, tab 120 in your own binder, sir. This is a letter from the CSB dated the 28th of July, 1992, signed by Mr. Krsto Savic, CSB chief, sent to the MUP of the Serbian Republic of BH, specifically to the minister. There's a reference there to a document dated the 26th of July. It reads: "With regard to the letter you sent to the Gacko SJB authorising senior police inspector Vojin Vukovic to set up a police station attached to the Gacko SJB, we hereby inform you of the following ..." Sir, what about this person, Vojin Vukovic, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a police administration inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know he wasn't from your own administration, but do you know that in the month of July he was off to Gacko to establish a police station there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, I think he did. I think there was even an incident that occurred or something like that, but I do remember him leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We best just read the document in its entirety to jog your memory. Mr. Savic goes on to say: "If there have been any mistakes or irregularities have been directly committed by members of the MUP at the Gacko police station, the Trebinje CSB must be informed so that together we can assess them and take adequate measures. "We have been told that the inspector who was given authorisation to set up the Gacko police station does not have the necessary respect and trust of the inhabitants of Gacko to carry out the given task. "In order to clarify the situation, we suggest that you send us detailed information of the reasons for 'setting up a police station' in Gacko and, if necessary, we can together deal with the situation and find a solution for it." Does this jog your memory in relation to what exactly occurred at Gacko?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I was saying. I remember some sort of an incident occurring there. Mr. Vukovic originally hails from Herzegovina. Why the animosity towards him in Gacko? I can't remember any details of the situation, but I know that some problems occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And do you perhaps know why Mr. Vukovic was dispatched to Gacko by the Ministry of the Interior, specifically the police administration?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, another team had previously been dispatched to Gacko. They drew up a report based on which the police administration ordered certain measures to be taken. I'm not sure if that was done following consultations with the head of the public security sector or not, but that would have been the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the previous team that travelled to Gacko had come up with anything? Your answer is not sufficiently clear the way it was recorded, and please try to speak slowly so the interpreters can understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The team of inspectors from the police administration visited the Gacko public security station. They ascertained that there were certain problems, which they presented in their report to the police administration leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that report in any way related to the fact that Inspector Vojin Vukovic was dispatched there to set up a police station in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police administration would have produced an assessment based on a report, following which they would dispatch an authorised inspector to help organise the situation and allow for a normal functioning of the public security station there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a couple of questions left. During his cross-examination, Mr. Hannis showed you P614.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have that up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch by the Presidency that you commented on when prompted by Mr. Hannis. You do remember that, sir, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, we have a case of war crimes against Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on the very end of this document in the Serbian, the last paragraph. If we could please have the same in English. It's on the next page of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As you see, sir, the Presidency is here adamant that information should be forwarded to the commission that we talked about, and then the reasons for that are stated. It reads: "This is very urgent because the enemy has established special offices or services to pass our victims off as their own. They then proceed to forward this information to all international organisations and embassies." Sir, did you know anything to indicate that this was really the case back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Zecevic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document you commented on with Mr. Hannis was P187, OTP tab 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have that on our screens, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember being shown this decision on the strategic objectives of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina by Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You answered about the extent of your knowledge and awareness of these strategic objectives. Nevertheless, sir, look at these six strategic objectives and tell us whether in your opinion - we're just waiting for the English to come up - in your opinion, is there a single strategic objective here that relates to the Ministry of the Interior and its members?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, the next document was P684, tab 115, OTP tab 115. This is a report on the work of the Prijedor SJB dated the 29th of September, 1992. You remember commenting on this document, sir, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, who would have been responsible for forwarding a report on the work of a certain SJB in a certain period of time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each of the CSBs in relation to their own areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the centres to draw up a report like that covering a certain time-period which is then to be forwarded to the Ministry of the Interior, would they not be required to gather all of the local reports from all of the public security stations throughout their area and then use those to draw up their own summary report, as it were? Is that not how it worked?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely how it worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are individual reports by each of the public security stations also individually forwarded to the ministry?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only report that is ever forwarded to the ministry is the CSB report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Two days ago, Mr. Hannis was showing you some military documents, specifically P591, tab 96, OTP tab 96; and P746, OTP tab 97. The former is a military security report and the latter is Colonel Sipcic's report, who at the time was a general, as the document tells us. You do remember being shown these two documents by Mr. Hannis, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, what about the Ministry of the Interior or your administration or indeed anyone else, did any of these ever receive any of the documents produced by the military back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about similar documents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 I don't remember receiving any documents from the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Macar. Mr. Macar, this concludes my re-examination. I would like to emphatically thank you for the time you have given us and for your effort in giving evidence here, particularly in view of your complex personal circumstances. We really appreciate your effort in coming here to help us establish facts. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to apologise for my breakneck pace at times and any omissions I may have made, but it was very difficult for me to control my speech at particular points in time and there was some misunderstanding due to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, I would like to go back to the Koricanske Stijene incident at the very end of August 1992. Charges were filed against unidentified persons. We've seen that, we've seen the document about that. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Were there ever charges filed against identified perpetrators? Against policemen? Reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I received back in 1993 suggested that we had been successful in identifying a number of persons, two, three, or more, I can't be sure. My information also suggested that these persons left and crossed to one of the VRS units. Some steps were taken and contacts established with some military security men in a bid to track these men down. Up until the end of 1995 no criminal reports had been filed against unknown [as interpreted] perpetrators, but one was still making an effort to both identify them and to physically track them down. That was the information that I had and that I had received from the centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I note that the witness said, line 21 and 22, that no criminal reports had been filed against known perpetrators until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, that's confusing because the rest of the answer goes on and says: "... but one was still making an effort to both identify them and track them down." So if there were known perpetrators, you don't need to identify them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you clarify that, Mr. Macar? You did say "known perpetrators," right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure says that first there would be criminal report against unknown perpetrators until the perpetrators are identified. Evidence is gathered to show that a certain person committed a certain criminal offence, and then one files a criminal report against a known perpetrator, which is then based on such material as has been forwarded to the prosecutor. At stage one we're talking about unknown perpetrators. What I stated is that up until the end of 1995, no criminal reports had been filed against known perpetrators because persons were not available who were suspected of committing a crime or there was circumstantial evidence to suggest that these persons committed a crime. I then went on to explain that the information that I had -- that I had received from the Banja Luka CSB - and I won't speculate whether we're talking about two or more persons - information was gathered about the possibility of their involvement in the commission of a crime, but they escaped to one of the VRS units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And those possible perpetrators that were identified, were there -- were they policemen from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We suspected some persons from Prijedor based on information received by the service. They were alleged to have been wearing what looked like police uniforms. Those too sported different colours sometimes, but our information suggested they were wearing uniforms and I can't speculate whether we're talking about two or more persons who were unavailable because they had escaped to some military units. Another thing that I do know is the services established contacts with the appropriate military authorities in a bid to locate those individuals, so that together with the military authorities we might bring these persons in for further procedure. That was the information that we had at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But even if the persons identified are at large but the investigators have information that they wear police uniforms, it must have been very easy to verify whether they were part of the police force, police officers or reserve police officers. Wouldn't that be an -- an easy, simple, and straightforward thing to establish?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was simple because in all stations, public security stations, they did not have orderly lists of reserve police force members. If you remember, when the Prosecutor put to me minutes of a collegium meeting from the end of 1993, the ministry was not properly equipped until quite late into the day when it comes to information, orderly information, for each member. This started in late 1993 and continued into 1994. It wasn't until then that they created the centralised database for all CSBs, SJBs, with the names of all members of active and reserve police force in order to establish the actual state of affairs and to eliminate consequences dating back or stemming from 1992, when the ministry was not able to establish exactly who the members were of active or reserve police force in a particular SJB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So although there was information that they were wearing police uniforms, what you're saying is it wasn't really helpful to check whether they were on the list, on a personnel list, of Prijedor police station or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I received early on in March when I attended the first meeting, I remember that I heard that there were two persons concerning whom there was some indicia. But the information did not point to them being members of either active or reserve police force. They continued on gathering information, and from the information coming from the site they were able to conclusively identify them. But I know that it wasn't until 1995 that they identified the entire group who had committed that terrible crime. Those initial two that were brought into custody, for them it was never with certainty established to which unit they belonged. And I think that it was only in late 1995 or 1996 that it was established that one of those suspected persons was killed in war operations. It was either in late 1995 or early 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It was established, wasn't it, that the incident happened with people, Muslim -- Muslims, on a convoy to Travnik; isn't that right? That was established quite early in September, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have stated earlier, I heard about the event for the first time in September, and it wasn't until March 1993 when the first meeting was held in the Banja Luka CSB in the crime police department that I was told - and I'm paraphrasing now based on what I can recollect - they told me that they were taking operative steps to try to identify the perpetrators. So it was only in March when I was briefed by the head of the crime police, I was inquiring about the state of affairs, and this is the information that I was given in March of 1993. Based on what he told me, I was sure, I was convinced that they were taking measures, adequate measures, and that this is how far they got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The investigations started immediately after the incident. Were they ever concluded properly, do you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard in March was that military representatives and representatives of judicial and civilian organs went to the site and that the civilian investigative judge from the court in Banja Luka continued acting on the case and that part of that team also comprised members of the Banja Luka CSB. The investigative judge from Banja Luka whose name I do not remember was in charge of that effort. After the consultations and after the first information became available, the investigative judge from Banja Luka whose name I cannot remember took over the case. According to the law, the investigative judge is the person in charge of the investigation and on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You didn't hear, you don't have any information about this investigation being interrupted, being stopped, being ordered to be stopped?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have information indicating that anybody had issued an order to terminate the investigation. The investigation is headed by the investigative judge, and I have no information indicating that anybody told them to terminate the investigation. I never heard of that either in 1993 or subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could the military authorities have ordered such a thing at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military authorities do not have jurisdiction over a civilian investigative judge, and I couldn't really speculate whether this judge acted in accordance with the law or not, whether he did what he was duty-bound to do under the law or not. Nobody could have ordered the judge to terminate the investigation or conduct any investigative measures without the consent of the judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether Stojan Zupljanin ever visited the crime site?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that particular piece of information, whether it was Mr. Zupljanin or somebody else representing the police who went to the site. I know that the event itself and the information about the event caused quite a big stir at the ministry. Everybody was upset. I know that I commented on this with my colleagues. Now, who came on behalf of the centre, whether it was Mr. Zupljanin or somebody else, I don't know. It is the investigative judge who sets up the investigative team and somebody from the centre is normally part of the team. Now, whether that person was Mr. Zupljanin or not, I can't tell you either way. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: At that time did you have within the MUP, central MUP, a forensic department?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 -- and by your leave I can explain. The forensic centre did not exist in Banja Luka in 1992. They started setting it up in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You're saying the forensic department in Banja Luka. I was asking about forensic department -- central forensic department within the service you were heading. Are we talking about the same thing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are discussing the same issue. In 1992 there was no forensic centre at the level of the Ministry of the Interior. It did not exist as part of the crime police administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I may refine the last question that Judge Delvoie put to you. Although this did not exist until 1993, was there an equivalent in 1992; and if not, who did the work which in 1993 came to be done by this central unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 in the CSB there was a forensic unit within the crime police sector. Head of that unit was Brane Buhovac, who later on was assigned to the position of the head of the forensic centre established by the headquarters of the Ministry of the Interior in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Hannis, anything arising out of the Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Actually, Judge, there are a couple of questions I would like to ask with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That would be fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, while the witness is on his way in, in addition to the question arising out of those put by the Bench yesterday you had indicated that you may have sought leave to re-open your cross-examination in terms of one point that Mr. Zecevic had opened on which you took objection. I assume that that matter has been resolved and you don't need to go down that road?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That had to do with something about a meeting that this witness had with Mr. Delimustafic. Based on his answer, I see no need to request re-examination on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought not. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, are you not aware that in -- as early as September and in October 1992, the Prijedor SJB by Mr. Drljaca had provided information to CSB Banja Luka Stojan Zupljanin about the policemen from Prijedor who had escorted the convoy from which these men were taken and murdered? You never knew about that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to see it, perhaps, but I don't know about these things. I didn't look at them and I don't remember learning about that back then. As part of the operative measures, they probably did seek information, which is only understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, this is in response to the question that Judge Delvoie asked you about: Wouldn't it be a simple and straightforward matter to find out who was in the police and who the police were that escorted that convoy?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I want to show two exhibits which were not on my list to use with this witness because I didn't anticipate this coming up, but they are in evidence and I would like to show the witness because they pertain. The first one is P682.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have a copy, Mr. Macar, so you'll have to look on the screen. It's dated the 24th -- or the 14th of September, from Mr. Drljaca to the chief of the CSB Banja Luka, responding to a dispatch that had been received from Banja Luka. And you will see it says: "In reference to your dispatch of the above number and date, we ... inform you we are unable to investigate the alleged killing on the 21st of August because all the policemen who escorted the convoy to Travnik have been in the battle-field in Han Pijesak since 9 September 1992." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're telling me this is the first time -- this is the first time you were aware that this information had been provided to Mr. Zupljanin in the CSB Banja Luka in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I was clear in my earlier evidence too. I learned of the event at Koricanske Stijene in September of 1992, as we were conducting preparations to move the headquarters of the ministry to Bijeljina. The first occasion to be briefed by the crime department of the CSB was in March. This is when the head of the crime department told me about what they had done. So that was in March, and as far as I can remember, they said that two or more suspects were in the VRS. It is possible that this is the same piece of information as mentioned in this letter. However, I never had occasion to see this letter before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But it's clear that the information about the names of the policemen involved in the escort were known back in September. Are you saying it was not possible to find two named known persons in the VRS? It wasn't like they had gone off and joined the French Foreign Legion.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a hypothetical question. In any unit, from Trebinje to Krupa, if a person --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're putting a hypothetical question to me. What I know is that despite the co-operation with the military organs, they were unable to establish where these two or three or more persons were, in which unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What information do you have that the names of these individuals were ever conveyed to the military by the police? Do you have any documents showing that was ever done?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I had [as interpreted] occasion to go to the archives of the ministry looking for some documents that I was interested in. In that meeting, as part of that meeting, I also inquired about Koricanske Stijene and I was told that they had established contact with the relevant military police persons and that they were working on trying to identify them. I can't now give you the number of the persons involved, whether it was two or more. They were trying to establish in which unit these people were in order to bring them in and to continue taking the necessary action in order to try to prove whether these persons had committed this crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe 23, 20, I believe the witness said in the negative, that he didn't have the opportunity to go to the archives of the ministry for the documentation that he was interested in. He mentioned the document from 2005 again. So maybe you can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't matter for the question I was asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The fact is, named perpetrators were known to the MUP, to Mr. Drljaca and Mr. Zupljanin, in September of 1992, but that information was not conveyed to any investigative judge or a prosecutor so that they could take the steps that they're entitled to do and able to do under the Law on Criminal Procedure. Right? They need that information before they can start initiating steps, and that information, although it was known by the police, was not conveyed to the prosecutor or a judge in 1992, was it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this letter, as far as I can understand, it says, all policemen who escorted the convoy to Travnik are on the battle-field in Han Pijesak. Now, whether all of them were perpetrators, whether all of them were suspected of perpetrating the crime, I don't know. I can't speculate on that. Perhaps some of them were suspected of having committed the crime. I don't even know how many policemen escorted the convoy and whether all of them were suspected of being involved in the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And those individuals' names were on payroll lists in the Prijedor SJB that were available to you or anyone else who wanted to look at them in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether all of them were on payroll lists, I don't know that. And I don't know how many policemen and who escorted the convoy. I didn't go into these details, either the payroll or anything else. I received information about what the CSB had done and what they were in the process of doing. Now, whether all of the escorts were suspected of having committed that crime or two or three or five of them were, I can't remember that. It somewhere stayed in my memory that two or more persons were suspected, but I don't know which persons. I was informed that they were trying to locate them via military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No further questions from me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just two, Your Honours, to clarify some issues concerning the question Mr. Hannis posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Macar, just a couple of questions. Who has jurisdiction over a crime which takes place in the territory of any CSB? Is it the centre that has jurisdiction over it or is it in the jurisdiction of the crime police administration in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administration in the headquarters does not deal directly with investigative measures. It is the jurisdiction of the centre and SJB to investigate actual crimes. In this particular case, it fell under the jurisdiction of the Banja Luka CSB in co-operation with the relevant public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the administration HQ did not have its own forensic team units or equipment. Even if the administration HQ had wanted to conduct an investigation, would they have had the means available to them to investigate serious crimes like these?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HQ-based crime administration did not have the organisational units that could have been used to shed light on complex crimes such as these. They didn't have a forensic centre, we didn't have a properly established and equipped organisational units to take special measures and document crimes, you probably know what that means, secret surveillance, tapping phone lines, conducting searches. And there is one thing that I would like to mention. In the Ministry of the Interior, not in 1992 and not during the war, we didn't have in -- the internal control service which now exists in all of the security bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, I beg you to focus on the question. We have half a page of your answer being recorded here, and I would like to again remind you of my question. Even if the administration, the HQ-based administration, had wanted to conduct an investigation, would you have had the means available to you or the services available to you to investigate serious crimes like these?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We didn't have the personnel, we didn't have the equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just another thing. When in March 1993 you were informed at the Banja Luka meeting about the then-status of the Koricanske Stijene case, were you briefed, were you presented a report, or did you inspect the files of the crime police of the Banja Luka CSB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not inspect the files. I was briefed by the relevant officer of the crime service there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that the established procedure in cases like these during -- during inspection rounds like these?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this was no inspection round or any inspection at all being carried out. This was our first meeting where we met the men in the leading positions of the crime service, the way the crime service was organised, the human resources situation, the equipment there; and we discussed the subjects of safety and crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for saying "inspection." It was my mistake, but please answer my question. Was that the established procedure during such visits for you to be briefed without you needing to go back and consult the files? Was that the established practice or did it just apply to this one situation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the established practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, I apologise, I should have asked you before I came to Mr. Zecevic as to whether you had any questions arising out of the Judges' questions, but I now ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honours, by the Chamber's leave I would like to ask a couple of questions in relation to Mr. Hannis' re-examination. I would also like to show the witness two additional documents if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you, Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: In relation to the document we have on our screens, the one you have been looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P1380.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: It says reference your dispatch such and such, the 9th -- the 11th of September. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Macar, this is the dispatch that we mentioned that Mr. Drljaca refers to in his reply. Likewise, Mr. Zupljanin is forwarding Mr. Stanisic's order here. If you look at the part just under Mico Stanisic's name, Mr. Zupljanin says: "In relation to this order, it is necessary to immediately take written statements about the events at Skender Vakuf, Knezevo, from the policemen that escorted the convoy from Prijedor to the border with Travnik on the 21st of August, 1992." And then it goes on: "You are to personally deliver the written statements with the biographical data on these policemen by the 15th of September at the latest. "You must also supply us with a list of all the citizens from your area who travelled on those convoys along the above-mentioned route at that time." You remember that previous document by Mr. Drljaca. The previous document does not, in fact, show that he acted upon this dispatch by Mr. Zupljanin and that he indeed forwarded all of the information required. Do you agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P617. Another dispatch by Mr. Zupljanin. Please zoom in on the Serbian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, again a dispatch by Mr. Zupljanin. Right at the outset he refers to two of his own previous dispatches. You remember the one dated the 11th of September and then the one by Mr. Simo Drljaca. Again, he demands, on the 7th of October, 1992, that Mr. Drljaca submit to him a detailed report to answer the following questions, and then there's a list of specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And it reads: "Inform me: "Which policemen escorted the convoy (personal details) ... (photocopy) ... and submit all of the -- and attach patrol orders, list all the policemen active and reserve who escorted the convoy." And then item 2: "Was anyone else, apart from the policemen, part of the convoy security and escort; and if so, who (personal details, what formation they belonged to and so on)?" Number 3: "What did the police officers write in their reports (patrol orders) when they returned from that mission (photocopy and attach reports from the service)?" Number 4: "The report on what was done during the on-site investigation ..." And at the very end, Mr. Zupljanin says: "I hereby again demand that you act upon and respond to our dispatch number ..." such and such, dated the 11th of September, 1992, the one that we looked at a minute ago. Mr. Macar, based on what I've just read back to you, based on what you've just seen, did Mr. Zupljanin not act perfectly in accordance with the law seeking to obtain all of the relevant information relating to the event from Mr. Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: The correction for the transcript, 30, 15, my question was: Did Mr. Zupljanin not act in accordance with the law in attempting to seek all the information relating to -- all the relevant information relating to the event from Mr. Simo Drljaca. My question was: Did Mr. Zupljanin act in accordance with the law in attempting to seek all the information relating to the event from Mr. Simo Drljaca. Thank you very much, Witness. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Aleksic, I was about to ask you whether you intended to show the witness Mr. Drljaca's report, the answer to this. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, do you know whether Mr. Drljaca ever responded to this dispatch? Did he write this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a document in evidence which I believe is that response, if you want to look; it's P618.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Further Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Macar, do you know whether Mr. Drljaca responded to this or -- except for what Mr. Hannis told you just right now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know whether he responded and whether he included any of the requested details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have on the screen P618, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But you have read it just now, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is this a proper response to Mr. Zupljanin's questions and his dispatch we just saw?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it contains everything that Mr. Zupljanin had requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: With regard to the information Mr. Zupljanin was looking at, was trying to get from Mr. Drljaca, would this have satisfied Mr. Zupljanin, do you think, or would you expect a further insistence from Mr. Zupljanin to get the information he wanted?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened later on during this exchange and as he was looking into the matter. I suppose he required further explanations because this document does not deliver what was previously requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And now that we know from Mr. Zupljanin's dispatches, the two of them, that the focus is on the policemen securing the convoy in something that even in those times must have been considered as a major incident and a terrible stain on the corps if ever they would have been involved. Would you expect this could end like this with two dispatches answered in a very evasive way and that would be it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is still my conviction that it didn't end like this, it couldn't have ended like this. But I don't think these two dispatches were all that it was about. It didn't end there. Now, what happened later, I can't say. I didn't have a chance to look at the actual exchange of letters or indeed to know about any operative steps that were taken. On the other hand, I can hardly speculate. I suppose there were further activities, and I believe that if you go to the archive of the CSB you should be able to find the relevant information there. I assume that this was not the end of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Macar, we thank you for coming to give evidence before the Tribunal, especially having regard to your particular circumstances. We know it's been a long period that you've been with us, and you are now released. And we wish you a safe journey back to your country and we also hope that your health issues are soon resolved. The -- I would remind Mr. Zecevic in your presence or remind you that Mr. Zecevic still has to provide for the benefit of the Tribunal, for the sake of completion, the necessary documentation in terms of the reason for why you would have been absent -- why we were unable to begin your testimony when we should have. So the usher would now escort you from the courtroom. Thank you again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours, for your attentiveness to my condition during the evidence. I would like to thank the Prosecutor as well and apologise to the Defence for my speedy evidence which may have left Mr. Zecevic at something of a disadvantage at times. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before I come to Mr. Hannis, who indicated he had two matters, there is -- well, one matter in two parts that the Chamber wishes to raise, part (b) of which should probably be in closed session. So we would do that now, we could move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You had foreshadowed, Mr. Zecevic, that the -- there will be a bar table motion filed on behalf of the accused Stanisic. Today is Wednesday and I am -- we are certain that you have this very much in hand, so could we expect this by Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We will file it by Friday, the bar table motion, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And you may -- the -- you may include -- the Chamber would also grant leave to include in that the matter which was dealt with in the brief private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. So do you now formally close, subject to that filing, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There is just one -- one additional matter. Your Honours' ruling -- the oral decision of 15th of July, 2011, in respect to one document which is 897D1, we intend to file a motion for reconsideration of the Trial Chamber on that particular -- on that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the -- and the -- oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, I was finished. I just said so noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, we would at this point close our case subject to our motion for reconsideration concerning the 897D1 and the bar table motion as we -- as we -- as we promised to be filed on Friday with -- with the addition of the matter which we discussed in the -- in the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just use the opportunity. We would like to express our gratitude to Ms. Veretelnikova and the Registry for their assistance and help. We would like to thank the VWS for their impeccable performance. We would like to thank the CLSS for the extra effort on translating some of the documents. And especially we are very grateful to the interpreters, which had a very hard time, I know, with some of our witnesses, for their exceptional and excellent job. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just, I guess, three brief matters. One is regarding Exhibit P2355, which is an organisational chart for the CSB Sarajevo. It was shown to the witness MS-003 and he made some changes and the Prosecution has now updated that chart with the changes, and that document is 65 ter 20217, reflecting the changes by MS-003. If there's no objection from the Defence and with the agreement of Your Honours, we would like to replace the old Exhibit P2355 with this new 65 ter 20217. I don't know if the Registry wants to give it the same number or -- okay. I see a nod of the head "yes" and that would be our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Basically the last thing you raised was what I was just about to ask of the Court Officer, whether it should be given a new number or whether we just substitute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, the -- according to the Court Officer, it's better to keep the old number. So the -- so -- so you may so substitute it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I've -- I'm sorry, I anticipated you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The second matter is just a matter in the transcript for 11 July, at page 23132, line 10, I am recorded as asking if we could show the witness Exhibit P991, which was tab 77 of our binder, a document dated 6th of March, and it -- the Exhibit is actually number P911, not P991. So perhaps I misspoke, but I wanted to correct that on the transcript. The last matter is that now the -- that we will be moving to the Zupljanin Defence case, we would request pursuant to Rule 67 that if -- that if the Zupljanin Defence have any statements of any of the witnesses that they intend to call, that those be provided to us in advance of the witnesses coming to testify sufficiently for us to prepare our cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, I'm sure that you're alive to that requirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, about the Cutileiro map, you remember yesterday or the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is there any agreement between parties about that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I didn't speak to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we haven't spoken, Mr. Hannis and I, but we -- we found out what apparently appears to be the case. In the -- in the annex report of our expert, Mr. Bajagic, in annex number 10 there was a map of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it is my understanding that the map of Bosnia and Herzegovina has been -- which is -- which is provided in that annex and is not part of the exhibit because we didn't offer the annex 10 is -- is quite different from the one that is -- well, quite different because it is different in -- in respect to -- to the municipalities and the -- a lot of information which was added by the Office of the Prosecutor. In any case, Your Honours, this -- this is -- both of these maps are basically the ethnic maps. They showed the ethnic majority of the certain population in the certain areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, it does not depict the -- the actual -- the actual Cutileiro Plan division on the -- on the -- on the -- on Bosnia-Herzegovina -- on the entities. And therefore, I don't know if that -- if that would be of much assistance to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So basically there is no agreement and let's forget about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, with regard to the Rule 67 matter, the Rule provides that the Trial Chamber should set a dead-line for that disclosure to be made, and I don't think one's been given to the Defence. We would like you to set a date so that there's no misunderstanding about when that material should be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Since you're on your feet, Mr. Hannis, could you assist by indicating when that dead-line should be in accordance with practice in the Rules?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think in a previous case I had it was -- it was 30 days before the witness was going to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, do you have a problem with 30 days?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would need to confer with my colleague, Mr. Krgovic. As far as I know, as far as I have learned over the last year, we did not take a single statement during all of our proofing sessions with our witnesses. I do have to check that with Mr. Krgovic and I shall certainly comply with any ruling by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that case, 30 days doesn't seem like too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, the -- rather than counsel from both sides and the Bench all being engaged in a guessing game at this point, this is certainly over the practice of the Tribunal and in accordance with the Rules such a well-trod path, that I'm sure that with very little research, counsel would know what they ought to do. So the Chamber would rule that counsel give the required notice in accordance with established practice, and that should cover it. And with that, we take the adjournment in this case to the 5th of September. I am sure that counsel on all sides would be diligently engaged in preparing for the next phase of this, but notwithstanding that work, that in such gap as there is and such breaks and you're able to take over the summer, I trust that everyone has a -- a safe time and come back refreshed and reinvigorated for the work ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of September, 2011

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.20 a.m.,
